research_conclusion: COST_ROBUST — the short-horizon momentum edge (lookback 3/5/10) survives the repository's realistic cost model (commission_per_trade=2.0, commission_per_share=0.003, slippage_cents=2.0, slippage_proportional=0.0005) and a 2x conservative stress with essentially unchanged candidate segment medians (cost drag at lookback 5 = 0.0000 for every asset with a baseline edge). Classification across the 10-asset universe: COST_ROBUST=6 (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA — exactly the previously-admitted lookback-robust set), NO_BASELINE_EDGE=4 (NVDA, JPM, JNJ, XOM), COST_FRAGILE=0, COST_ERASES_EDGE=0. Costs are genuinely charged (e.g. AAPL realistic commission $18.7k over 4452 constant-dollar rebalancing fills; full-sample total return +553.0% zero -> +551.4% realistic) but small relative to the multi-percent per-fold edge. Qualification: robustness follows from low turnover (~1 sign flip/asset over 2009-2026; a persistent long bias), not a high-turnover timing alpha; the regime-verdict machinery is null-dispersion-sensitive. Exploratory research simulation, not a traded idea.
